questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Cofactor Method To Solve for an Unknown Quantity
questions.problem:
The entry ${a}_{12}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ k & 6 & 0\end{aligned}]$
equals $18.$ Find the value of $k.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A)=|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ k & 6 & 0\end{aligned}| & =1|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ k & 0\end{aligned}|+3|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ k & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(0-24)-2(0-4k)+3(0-k) \\  & =8k-3k-24 \\  & =5k-24.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{12}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{21}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{21} & =(-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(0-18) \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{12}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{21} \\  & =\frac{1}{5k-24}\cdot 18 \\  & =\frac{18}{5k-24}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{13}^{′}=18$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{18}{5k-24} & =18 \\ \frac{1}{5k-24} & =1 \\ 1 & =5k-24 \\ 25 & =5k \\ k & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating an Element of the Inverse of a 3x3 Matrix
questions.problem: Determine the entry ${a}_{33}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix $A$ $=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & -3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}A=|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & -3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}| & =5|\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|-0|\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|+3|\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =5(0-2)+0+3(-2+3) \\  & =-10+0+3 \\  & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since we want the entry ${a}_{33}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{33}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{33} & =(-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-15-0 \\  & =-15.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{33}^{′}=\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{33}=\frac{1}{-7}\cdot (-15)=\frac{15}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Determine the entry ${a}_{21}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}A=|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}| & =2|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}|-4|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(0+9)-4(0-6)+1(0+2) \\  & =18+24+2 \\  & =44.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since we want the entry ${a}_{21}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{12}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{12} & =(-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(0-6) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{21}^{′}=\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{12}=\frac{1}{44}\cdot 6=\frac{3}{22}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The entry ${a}_{23}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 2 & k & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]$
equals $\frac{1}{2}$ and $det(A)=k-1.$ Find the value of $k.$

$k=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, note that we are given the determinant of $A:$

$$
det(A)=k-1
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{23}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{23}^{t}={c}_{32}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{32} & =(-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(-1+2) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{23}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{23}^{t} \\  & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{32} \\  & =\frac{1}{k-1}\cdot (-1) \\  & =-\frac{1}{k-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{23}^{′}=\frac{1}{2}$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{k-1} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ k-1 & =-2 \\ k & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The entry ${a}_{23}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 2 & k & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]$
equals $\frac{1}{4}$ and $det(A)=-2k-3.$ Find the value of $k.$

$k=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, note that we are given the determinant of $A:$

$$
det(A)=-2k-3
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{23}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{23}^{t}={c}_{32}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{32} & =(-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(1+2) \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{23}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{23}^{t} \\  & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{32} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-2k-3)}\cdot (-3) \\  & =\frac{3}{\,2k+3\,}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{23}^{′}=\frac{1}{4}$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\,2k+3\,} & =\frac{1}{4} \\ 12 & =2k+3 \\ 2k & =9 \\ k & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
